newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt and futures lower in market downturn.
newsitem.headline: German debt and futures lower in market downturn.

text.p: German Bunds and futures were lower in late dealings on Tuesday, hurt by what traders described as a minor market correction and technical chart factors that favoured selling.

At 1505 GMT, DTB September Bund futures were down 39 basis points at 102.28 points while the 10-year 6.00 percent cash Bund due July 2007 was at 102.73 with a yield of 5.63 percent compared with the close on Monday at 103.03.
The firmer dollar and weaker U.S. debt prices added to the market's troubles as traders wondered how long the selling pressure will remain in the market.

"It's hard to say right now how the market is going to develop," said one trader. "It is possible that the losses may stop here. The technical factors are showing that we are starting to build a base."
But others said September Bunds broke key support at 102.30 and 102.15 and that the market was looking vulnerable for a breakdown to 102.00.
"Staying bearish below 102.53 is favoured, the double top objective at 101.91," market consulting group MMS International said in a commentary.
Traders paid little attention that the Bundesbank would return to a variable-rate repo tender at its next council meeting a week from Thursday due to the strong dollar.
"I think the speculation was exaggerated," said one trader. "It was clear that the market needed a correction and to stop the upward trend in prices for a bit."

Instead, MMS said its survey showed traders expect very little change in Bundesbank policy and that the weak mark does not seem to be a factor since domestic prices are subdued and imported price inflation is not seen as a danger.
